the BFKL resummation of ln(1/x) terms is essential for a quantitative description of single particle production at large $p^2_T$ in DIS at small x.
(a) DIS + jet events at HERA are described by BFKK dynamics and that (b) the shape of the DIS + jet events is well described by BFLK dynamics.

the BFKL resummed calculation is in better agreement with the DIS + jet data than the calculation with the BFKK resummation omitted, and that the BFKK ln(1/x) resummed calculation describes the DIS + jet x distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transverse momentum distribution of particles produced in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data support a picture of the dynamics of DIS at small $x$ in which the $ln$ (1/x) evolution is dominated by the BFKL mechanism.
the data support the BFKL resummation at large $p_t$ and small x.
the $p_T$ distribution is a probe of the small x dynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data favour BFKL dynamics for DIS with a large momentum transfer.
the BFKL dynamics is favoured over the DGLAP dynamics at small x.
the BFKL resummation is needed in DIS to describe both the shape and normalization of the $p_T$ spectrum and the shape of the x spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DIS + jet data are sensitive to the dynamics at small x.
the BFKL dynamics are relevant for small $x$ physics in DIS.
the $p_T$ spectrum of DIS in the central region is sensitive to the BFKL resummation and can be used to probe the small x dynamics.
